key_insight: The paper proposes a self-evolving, expert-in-the-loop framework that uses LLM assistance plus expert verification to produce DSM-5-TR-aligned, explainable depression annotations with traceable evidence.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical annotation pipeline for building auditable mental-health datasets that can improve XAI model reliability and reduce manual labeling effort.
method: Select candidate evidence from textual records
Perform criterion-level DSM-5-TR analysis with LLM assistance and expert review
Synthesize case-level labels and use Example Memory + Reflection Memory to incorporate feedback without retraining
evidence_signal: A pilot study on expert-reviewed samples reports improved annotation consistency and explainability while reducing manual revision effort, but broader multi-cycle evaluation is deferred.
watch_item: The framework’s benefits are currently shown only in a pilot setting, and its iterative feedback mechanism still needs validation across multiple annotation cycles and datasets.
paper_title: Self-Evolving Human-Centered Framework for Explainable Depression Symptom Annotation
